How to revise

The author uses this approach to keep philosophy, personal understanding, and actual work connected as they change. Revision can begin with a developed idea, changed circumstances, an objection, or an arrangement that no longer fits. Find what has changed, work through its consequences, and let the result correct the understanding that guided the change.

Adapt the approach to your purpose, materials, and environment. You may be writing a different philosophy, revising one personal interpretation, or changing a tool. The connections below help identify what needs attention; their order and extent follow the work. The method itself can also be revised when experience shows a better way to proceed.

Write your own actual revision method

Write the method fitted to your practice at references/situated/revision.md in the private package. This guide explains how to write it; the author's approach below offers adaptable material.

Explain what prompts revision, how relevant philosophy and personal material are obtained, how local scope and connected changes are judged, and how environmental changes reach a checked result. Name usable materials and routes, and the judgments needing your participation. A new philosophy, no website, or different working conditions can change the approach. Let the actual method express these conditions instead of reproducing another author's environment.

Scope and connected changes

Identify the result sought and the part that needs development. Distinguish the revision focus, the material used to judge it, and other parts that need to change. Reading philosophy to assess an interface does not itself select the philosophy for rewriting.

Current focus Corresponding work
Refresh personal Yinyang and its environment Reconsider personal material in light of philosophy and current sources, assess the connected accounts, then inspect the relevant Skills and arrangements.
Revise a philosophical claim or personal interpretation Develop the passage and follow changes in meaning into the accounts, methods, or representations that depend on it.
Repair a Skill, page, tool, or arrangement Diagnose and fix that object. Return to a premise or personal interpretation if the result exposes a mistake there.

Follow substantive changes through their actual dependencies. A wording or presentation correction may finish at its source and reading surface; a changed division of work may also require changing the instructions that implement it. Preserve an explicit stopping boundary and explain any necessary consequence that remains unfinished.

Establish the current material

Read the relevant philosophy and working accounts, then select supporting material for the question. Locate maintained originals and distinguish them from summaries, generated copies, and published versions. Check what is actually available and identify access gaps that affect the judgment.

Purposes, research directions, relationships, and conditions may have changed since an account was written. Compare its sources with current exchange. The model can retrieve, compare, investigate, and write; the person contributes experience and judgments unavailable in those materials. Use what they have already supplied.

Write for the actual use

State relevant objects, relations, evidence, conditions, responsibilities, and consequences in clear language. Distinguish a reported experience, an interpretation, a chosen commitment, and an operational requirement where they would lead to different judgments or actions. Personal information supplies contextual evidence; its presence in an account does not make it a command.

Use direct expression. A philosophical distinction or literary image can clarify a relation; explain its meaning where that relation should guide work. Preserve original expression as attributable material while making the maintained interpretation and practical consequences explicit. Keep extended philosophical arguments at their own source and link them where useful.

Sources and evidence

Choose personal writing, conversation, memory, observed work, and philosophical material because they bear on the question. Retain source identity, time, relevant passages, and enough context to assess consequential claims. Where a summary mediates access to an original, make that relation visible: its selection and omissions can shape an interpretation.

Different materials support different claims. A person's report grounds what they expressed or experienced in context; an explanation offered with it still needs assessment. Observed work shows what happened under inspected conditions. A chosen commitment states a direction; philosophy contributes concepts and reasons. In a fictional reading example, reporting greater ease supports experienced ease, and reaching the right passage supports access. Lasting learning and the cause of improvement need further evidence.

Keep temporal scope and uncertainty intelligible. Later speech may correct an interpretation, describe a new situation, or introduce unresolved conflict. Explain important inferences: what supports them, why the connection matters, and what limits their use. Several summaries of one source add no independent support.

Keep extended episodes and unique originals with their existing owners; give derived accounts usable locators and grounds. In the author's package, the private source entrance is references/personal/sources.md; the package guide explains its placement. Preserve useful originals while retiring redundant summaries. Access for revision does not authorize unrelated personal collection or public disclosure of private quotations, portraits, or unpublished work.

Let philosophy revise personal support material

Bring developed philosophy into contact with existing personal material. Which interpretations does it clarify? Which distinctions were missing? Which summaries now mislead? Rewrite derived material so experience, interpretation, chosen direction, and uncertainty remain intelligible. Philosophy helps formulate understanding; attributable expression and actual use ground its personal application.

When a public argument is already maintained elsewhere, link it and retain the private meaning and evidence that this account needs. This keeps the support useful as the philosophy changes.

Let philosophy and personal material revise working accounts

Read the philosophy alongside refreshed personal evidence. In the author's Yinyang, orientation articulates adopted values and direction; person grounds understanding of the actual person; counterpart relates available capacity to wanted contribution; relationship explains joint activity; environment explains its realization. The writing guides develop these different responsibilities.

Preserve supported substance and rewrite the relations that changed. Distinguish preference from explanatory hypothesis, wanted role from demonstrated capability, and selected arrangement from observed effect. Read neighboring accounts together so the revision remains coherent. Either participant can generate, object, reason, and revise.

Reconsider the actual revision method too. If it repeatedly creates unnecessary work, obscures a judgment, or fails to carry a change into use, revise the relevant guidance and check whether the new approach helps. Another person's practice can call for different objects, organization, or methods.

The person rereads the six accounts and recurring patterns

The person can read and reflect on the six actual accounts: orientation, person, counterpart, relationship, environment, and revision. The model helps locate relevant passages, connect particular experiences, and develop candidate explanations. The person can recognize fit or mismatch, offer exceptions, or reconsider an earlier purpose. Select accounts by the current question and keep their sources accessible.

One path brings authored philosophy to personal descriptions and their realization: how do these explanations understand self and others, what life does the arrangement support, and which values and concepts need revision too? Another begins with recurring experiences, comparing what happened, how the person understood the other, what response they expected, and how their own actions participated in the resulting relationship. Examine actual demands, conditions, and dependencies alongside the proposed relational explanation.

Both paths treat the files themselves as revisable accounts. Retain competing explanations and counterexamples. Where conditions permit and the person wishes, connect a new understanding with a possible expression, action, or adjustment to collaboration, then revise affected accounts and environment through actual consequences. Rereading one's patterns develops the philosophical and psychoanalytic resources. A clearer account, a new personal understanding, and lasting relational or lived change require their respective evidence. Record what has changed and what remains to be understood accordingly.

Let the whole Yinyang revise Skills and the environment

Use the connected philosophy and personal understanding to assess the Skills and arrangements relevant to the intended result. Do their purposes, instructions, examples, resources, and actual behavior support the contribution wanted? Include prompts, tools, and interfaces where their dependencies affect it. Specialist Skills retain their own methods and task responsibilities.

Repair actual mismatches: contradictory instructions, inaccessible context, an unsuitable interface, or machinery whose contribution has disappeared. Remove displaced guidance and keep what still works. The environment writing guide develops realization; use your environment's actual authoring, implementation, and publication routes.

Make webpage revisions visible before publication

The author's practice includes a public website. When revising its diagrams, the model shows the changed diagrams in the conversation. For a new or substantially changed page, it shows a readable rendering of the actual unpublished version and explains consequential changes before publishing. A further material edit calls for an updated preview of that version.

This lets the person encounter the work while it can still change. Already authorized publication continues, incorporating feedback when it arrives; personal authentication, consent, and explicit stopping boundaries keep their scope. A practice without a website can use the relevant equivalent: read a draft, try an interface, or inspect a work before sharing it.

Follow the result back into understanding

Compare a summary with its evidence, a generated copy with its source, and a completion claim with the result reached through the actual entrypoint. An unavailable account calls for delivery repair; an account faithfully followed but producing an unsuitable contribution calls for examining its meaning or the selected relationship.

Carry authorized changes through the affected sources and consumers, then read back what is available to the intended reader or working model. Where copies depend on an authored source, update them through their actual route. Keep private material within its authorized audience.

Compare the intended result with the observable outcome and explain required differences still open. Return to personal material, working accounts, or philosophy when evidence challenges them. Useful output, collaborative fit, and personal development have different grounds; let the claim match what the revision and subsequent use actually establish.
